name: Deschutes County
tax_rate: 8% unincorporated county TLT (6% + 1% 1988 + 1% 2014) plus 1.5% state; cities levy their own in place of the county rate
deadline_pattern: Applications open the first week of January and close mid-February (Feb 16, 2024; Feb 13, 2026); recipients announced in April; 12-month grant period starting May 1. The 2027 round reopens January 4, 2027; deadline not yet posted
typical_open: First Monday of January (Jan 8, 2024; Jan 5, 2026; Jan 4, 2027 per VCO funding page)
annual_pool: $300,000 in 2026 (12 projects); $280,000 in 2025 (7 projects); $450,000 in 2024 (15 projects); about $840,000 in the 2023 launch round. 2027 pool not announced
contact: Future Fund inbox grants@visitcentraloregon.com; Scott Larson, CEO, Visit Central Oregon, scott@visitcentraloregon.com, 541-389-8799. Program administered for VCO by Rural Prosperity Partners
notes: Deschutes County does not run its own open grant round; county TLT goes to the Sheriff, Central Oregon Visitors Association (Visit Central Oregon) and Fair & Expo marketing. The outside-applicant program is the Central Oregon Future Fund, which VCO funds from county TRT and Travel Oregon RCTP dollars and opens each January for projects in Deschutes, Jefferson, Crook and South Wasco counties. Awards are judged against three pillars (stewardship, cultural tourism, access adventure) by seven to eight advisory reviewers, with priority points for off-peak season (Oct 1 to the Friday before Memorial Day), multi-jurisdiction impact and a 10% cash match; typical requests are $20,000 to $50,000 and for-profits are eligible. The pool has fallen from $840,000 to $300,000 in four years, and 26 applicants sought over $1 million in 2026.
members_source: https://ktvz.com/news/local-news/2026/04/28/12-regional-tourism-projects-awarded-grants-by-visit-central-oregon-totaling-300k/ (eight unnamed advisory reviewers from tourism, hospitality, media, outdoor recreation, rural communities and Warm Springs)

presentation.pattern: No applicant presentation; VCO hosts informational and project-development webinars in early January
presentation.format: Online application portal; reviewers score written applications

meeting_schedule: No public committee; VCO advisory reviewers score in March, status notices early April, contracts late April, funds released May 1
pool_note: County collected $12,714,324 in FY2024-25 (est. $13.37M current). The first 6% splits 80% Sheriff/county and 20% COVA; the 1988 1% goes to COVA; the 2014 1% is 70% Fair & Expo marketing. None of that is open to outside applicants. The only competitive dollars are the Future Fund ($300,000 in 2026), which VCO funds from its TRT share plus Travel Oregon RCTP money, so the $300,000 is not purely Deschutes County TLT.

name: Cannon Beach
tax_rate: 8% city (9% proposed in a 2025-26 council work session) plus 1.5% state; Clatsop County 3% applies per the source list
deadline_pattern: Spring window for the following fiscal year: the FY2024-26 round opened May 3 and closed June 7, 2024; the Tourism and Arts Commission's FY2026-27 recommendations went to City Council on August 6, 2026. Expect a May-June 2027 window for FY2027-28
annual_pool: Not published online; a city work session estimated about $385,000 a year in tourism-restricted TLT, of which $160,000 funds the Visitor Information Center and about $220,000 covers other tourism uses including the Tourism and Arts Fund
contact: City of Cannon Beach, City Hall, 163 E Gower, P.O. Box 368, Cannon Beach OR 97110; no named TAF staff contact published (community grants went through Kelsey Balensifer, balensifer@ci.cannon-beach.or.us, in 2022)
notes: The Tourism and Arts Fund (TAF) is the city's TLT grant program; the five-member Tourism and Arts Commission writes the guidelines, reviews applications and sends award recommendations to City Council, which approved the FY2026-27 awards by motion on August 6, 2026. The commission describes the fund as money local nonprofit groups use to promote tourism and the arts, so for-profit event producers should expect to partner with a nonprofit. The city website returned errors for the TAF application page, finance reports and the August 2026 packet during this research, so the pool, award list and 2027 dates are unconfirmed even after a second pass through Daily Astorian and Gazette coverage (no award article found); a separate city Community Grants program ($175,000 to 20 groups in 2025) is general-fund money, not TLT.
meeting_schedule: Tourism and Arts Commission meets as needed, 9:00 AM in Council Chambers (next listed: Monday, November 16, 2026); council acts on award recommendations in summer (Aug 6, 2026)
pool_note: Est. $4.27M city TLT. State law restricts 70% of post-2003 increments to tourism; the city's own estimate for the proposed 1% increase was about $385,000 tourism share per point-equivalent year, with $160,000 to the visitor center. The TAF grant pool itself was not retrievable (city PDFs blocked), so competitive dollars are unknown.

name: Astoria
tax_rate: 11% city plus 1.5% state; Clatsop County 3% applies per the source list
deadline_pattern: Applications due the last Friday of February at 5:00 PM for the fiscal year starting July 1 (Feb 28, 2025; Feb 27, 2026); applicants present to the Budget Committee in early March; awards final when council adopts the budget in June. Expect a late-February 2027 deadline for FY2027-28
typical_open: January, when the Finance Department mails invitation letters
annual_pool: Two programs from the Promote Astoria Fund: (1) Funding for Promotion, Development and Services Supporting Tourism, amount set in the budget (last cycle: Chamber $183,653, ADHDA $120,000, Uppertown $69,000); (2) Arts and Culture Program to Promote Tourism, up to $100,000 for FY2026-27
contact: Ryan Quigley, Assistant to the City Manager, rquigley@astoria.gov, City of Astoria, 1095 Duane Street, Astoria OR 97103; invitation letters issued by Hilary Norton, Finance Director
notes: Astoria runs two TLT-funded grant rounds each winter out of the Promote Astoria Fund, and the Budget Committee (council plus appointed citizens) sets the amounts during the budget process rather than a tourism committee. The tourism-organization program mostly re-funds the same four groups each year (Chamber visitor center, Downtown Historic District Association, Uppertown Business Association, Travel Alliance), while the Arts and Culture program (up to $100,000) is the realistic entry point for an outside event. Applicants must attend the March Budget Committee meeting for a five-minute presentation plus five minutes of questions, be a 501(c) or apply through one, and file semi-annual reports; funds are reimbursement-based.

The Arts and Culture program, capped at $100,000 for FY2026-27, is the portion realistically open to new applicants.

tax_rate: 9% city plus 1.5% state (DOR table also shows a 10% listing); Linn County 3% applies per the source list
deadline_pattern: Applications accepted July 1 through September 1 (11:59 PM) every year; the Tourism Advisory Committee reviews in September and may open a second round if funds remain
annual_pool: $50,000 per year of the city biennium (Collaborative Tourism Promotion grant)
contact: Jennifer Wehr, Economic Development Program Coordinator, jennifer.wehr@albanyoregon.gov, 541-791-0180 (page contact box also lists Sophie Adams, sophie.adams@albanyoregon.gov, 541-917-7550); mail to 333 Broadalbin Street SW, P.O. Box 490, Albany OR 97321
notes: Albany's Collaborative Tourism Promotion (CTP) grant sets aside $50,000 a year of TLT for new events, new marketing campaigns, convention bids and placemaking, with the Tourism Advisory Committee making the final decision by majority vote. Applicants submit a five-page application with vendor quotes (one quote under $10,000, three above) and attend the committee meeting in person to describe the project; wages, alcohol, marijuana and tobacco are excluded and repeat requests are discouraged. The bulk of Albany's TLT goes to the Albany Visitors Association under contract, so $50,000 is the competitive ceiling.

pool_note: Est. $1.06M city TLT. Finance Policy F-12-12-001 routes the tourism share to the Albany Visitors Association contract and city purposes; the CTP grant is fixed at $50,000 per year.

notes: Silverton's Tourism Promotion Committee, formed in 2008, runs spring and fall TLT grant cycles and recommends awards to City Council, which approves them about a month after each deadline. In March 2024 the city and the Sutherlin Area Chamber held a town hall introducing a community fund open to individuals and organizations proposing local projects; the chamber is the practical door for TLT support. The city manager said in June 2025 that the city and chamber spend TLT dollars jointly, and cited Blackberry Festival costs while supporting HB 3962, so expect a general-fund tilt once HB 4148 takes effect.
pool_note: FY2025-26 budget: $317,500 transient room tax, all into the Tourism-Motel Tax Fund ($365,000 appropriated incl. $85,000 capital, $25,000 transfer to general fund). No line item for outside grants; the chamber community fund amount is unpublished.

name: St. Helens
tax_rate: 10% city plus 1.5% state; Columbia County proposed 4% in St. Helens under Measure 5-314 (Nov 3, 2026 ballot)
contact: City of St. Helens Tourism Program (Tourism Director position, most recently Tina Curry); Finance Director Gloria Butsch; city events produced under contract by Treadway
notes: St. Helens runs its TLT through a city Tourism Fund that produces its own events (Spirit of Halloweentown with a roughly $1.2M budget, 13 Nights on the River, Independence Day, Christmas Ships tree lighting, Sand Island Sandcastle Competition) under a contracted event company, Treadway, rather than granting to outside applicants. The fund hit a $350,000 shortfall in September 2026 that council covered with a $250,000 contingency transfer and a $100,000 loan, so new outside requests are unlikely in FY2026-27. Columbia County's Measure 5-314, which would have layered a 4% county TLT inside St. Helens, was failing 73% to 27% in Nov 3, 2026 early returns.
pool_note: Est. $123K city TLT; the Tourism Fund is dominated by event revenue and sponsorships for city-produced events and had a $350,000 gap in 2026. No competitive grant dollars.

name: Enterprise
tax_rate: 5% city motel tax (city grant packet; source list shows 3%) plus Wallowa County 5% and 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: Applications due March 1 and September 1 at 3:30 PM; applicants present in person to City Council the second Monday of March or September at 6:30 PM; awards announced the second Monday of April or October
typical_open: Rolling; packets available year-round from City Hall
annual_pool: Not published; maximum $2,000 per applicant per grant cycle (events outside city limits capped at 20% of that)
contact: Zak Bradshaw, City Administrator/Recorder, zbradshaw@enterpriseoregon.gov, 541-426-4196 x3, 102 E. North St., Enterprise OR 97828
notes: Enterprise runs the Hotel/Motel Tax (CETRA, Community-Economic-Tourism Related Activities) grant twice a year from its city and county motel tax share, for special events, tourism promotion, downtown enhancement and public beautification. Applicants submit seven paper copies plus a digital copy by March 1 or September 1, must present in person to City Council for 10 minutes (applications not presented in person are not considered), then the Motel Tax Committee reviews and council votes the following month; awards are capped at $2,000 per cycle and a follow-up report is due within 30 days. For-profit ventures and individuals are excluded, so a business-run event needs a nonprofit or public sponsor; priority goes to projects generating overnight stays, local business support and media coverage.
members_source: Motel Tax Committee reviews and recommends; roster not published on the city grants page

name: Bay City

contact: City of Bay City, City Manager (applications to City Hall or by email per committee notice); ci.bay-city.or.us/forms
notes: Bay City has a council-appointed TLT Committee that reviews tourism-related grant applications and advises council on use of its roughly $22,000 a year in TLT, meeting one to two times a quarter; no application form, deadline or pool is published online, so treat it as a small rolling request to City Hall. The city's 2022 destination management plan earmarks its TLT for website, social media, concerts and festivals, interpretive signage and small capital items, and the city itself won a county facilities grant for the Al Griffin Park campground. Larger asks go to the Tillamook Coast Visitors Association programs (facilities grant, marketing grants, $2,500 event sponsorships for September to May events).
